description:
Two Finger Gripper: delete Gen 15 (Two Finger Gripper/versions/v015_generalist_printable) and make a new v015 that improves on v014_generalist_tip_contact. Jake (voice, looking at the HelpingHands Live Preview design gallery): "Delete version 15, we don't need it. Then make a new version 15 that improves on version 14: the actual gripper part at the end, past the black dots (from where the finger would stop, where it bumps out, to the tip), should be much longer. In the reference it looks like about a third of the total length, so extend that end section to roughly a third of the length."

Notes for the implementer:
- Reference photos: cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_closed.png and the other generalist photos v014's README uses; 'black dots' is probably v014's dark tip pad / the bump where the finger stops. Confirm against the photos.
- 3D designs use the dual render: a three.js vision render plus an OpenSCAD STL from the same angles, diffed. The STL is the source of truth.
- The new v015 must appear in the Live Preview gallery (Scripts/publish_designs.py discovery -> ~/HelpingHands-tools/design-gallery catalog) in place of the deleted one. Update VERSIONS.txt.
- Heads-up: v016_generalist_simple is built from Gen 15's fingers. Removing the old v015 must not break v016 (copy over or re-point anything it imports); leave v016 in place.

results.identified_issue: Interpretation: 'thick end section' = the generated beak from the black dot (trace_photo.py DOT_XY, z=82.1 mm) to the point. By plan-view width the head from the shoulder bump (z~70) was already ~33%, so that reading would have meant no change; the dot->point section (23%) matches Jake's 'much longer' and the closed photo's ~38%. Mechanism: NEEDLE['TIP'] is moved via stretch_z (z past the dot x1.7, x kept), so needle_frame/closed_jaw regenerate the beak and the contact is still shaped in mm. Slots remapped by fraction of beak length and width (beak_slots); holes filter uses the photo slot positions (otherwise a slot blob became a stray hole). Recalibrated: ROUND_BACK 0.4->1.0 (mesh innermost reach z 123.35 vs trace tip 124.31), contact_back -0.028->+0.001 (mesh reach 27.2507 vs trace 27.2500), WEDGE 4deg/0.35->4.5deg/0.40 (on-target 4/0.35 gives 5.7deg in the 1-2 mm window; Gen 14 passed at 6.6 only because its contact lagged 0.6 mm). check_geometry gap_profile now slices triangles at z instead of a +-0.25 mm vertex window (beak vertices ~0.9 mm apart). Raising needle n to 82 broke watertightness, so n stays 48. Arm kept fixed, so the finger is 16% longer; the alternative (keep total length, compress the arm) was not chosen. Gallery verified via publish_designs.py --no-build into a scratch dir (not the live gallery) + test_gripper_poses against that catalog. Not done: three.js concept/dual render (pipeline doesn't cover these versions), stiffness, print.
results.summary: Old Gen 15 is deleted. The new Gen 15 is Gen 14 with the thick beak 1.7× longer, so it's now a third of the finger.
results.detailed_description:
The new Gen 15 (v015_generalist_long_jaw) is Gen 14 with the beak stretched 1.7×. That's the thick end section, from the black dot to the point. It goes from 25 mm (23% of the finger) to 42 mm (33%). The finger grows from 109 to 127 mm. Everything behind the dot is unchanged. The point stays where it was sideways, so the beak gets longer and a bit slimmer, not wider. The six slots spread out along it. You were right about the photos: in the closed photo that section is about 38% of the finger, so Gen 14's was short.

Only the points still touch when it closes. The slimmer point needed two small re-tunes: the V behind the point is now 4.5° per side to 0.40 mm (Gen 14 used 4° to 0.35 mm), and the pivots sit at ±27.25 mm. All geometry and mesh checks pass. Gen 16 copied everything it needed, so it still passes its checks too. It now shows as Gen 15 in the Live Preview gallery, in place of the old one. Have a look at previews/compare_gen14.png for Gen 14 next to Gen 15 at the same scale.

One heads-up: there's no three.js concept render for this. The web-vs-STL diff tool only covers cad/openscad designs, and no Two Finger Gripper generation has one. The gallery draws the STLs directly. Nothing is printed yet, and a longer, slimmer beak will flex more at the tip.

results.notes: Correction from Jake (this REPLACES the 'past the black dots' wording above; ignore that part): the section to lengthen is the end section from where the gripper starts getting much thicker, out to the tip. That thick end section should be quite a bit longer, about a third of the total finger length. Check this against the reference images (cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_closed.png and the other generalist photos); Jake thinks they show that thick section much longer than v014 has it. Everything else in the request stands: delete old v015, new v015 improves on v014, dual render (three.js vision render + OpenSCAD STL, same angles, diffed, STL is truth), shows in the Live Preview gallery in place of the old v015, keep v016 working.

summary: Delete the old Two Finger Gripper v015 and build a new v015 from v014 whose thick end section, from where it thickens to the tip, is much longer. That section should be about a third of the finger length per the reference photos, with v016 still working and the new v015 shown in the Live Preview gallery.
